correctness.rationale: Every centered affine-regular hexagon has vertices ±u, ±v, ±(v-u) and area three times the absolute determinant of u and v. Exact facet enumeration for the unit-circumradius regular octagon leaves precisely three positive-orientation chambers after dihedral normalization; each determinant is a convex quadratic. Exact endpoint and critical-point evaluation gives the claimed common minimum and maximum, and the middle chamber continuously realizes the full interval.
risks: The symbolic checker is finite and exact; no numerical experiment is used to infer the universal bound.

value.rationale: The source paper is explicitly about minimum and maximum area affine-regular hexagons, and it distinguishes constant-area bodies such as parallelograms. The regular octagon is a canonical highly symmetric non-parallelogram test case. Computing its complete area interval supplies a natural exact benchmark for that theory, demonstrates quantitatively how close it is to the constant-area phenomenon, and packages the optimization into three transparent quadratic chambers.
risks: The value is a canonical special-body benchmark rather than a general theorem for all centrally symmetric bodies.
